subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi John — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + our recommended next steps and model shortlist based on the use cases you described (support summarization + high-throughput embeddings for search):

Summary of needs from today:
- Real-time chat summarization (95th perc latency target ~180ms)
- Batch embeddings for nightly ingestion (cost-sensitive)
- Strong guardrails for PII handling and audit logs

Recommended shortlist (attached PDF):
1) redwood-llama-70b-quant (recommended default) — best quality/latency balance for your long-form summarization prompts; good SSE cost with 16-bit quantized variant.
2) redwood-realtime-13b (low-latency variant) — meets the 95th perc latency target in our infra tests; slightly lower ROUGE on long summaries but much cheaper per-token.
3) open-embed-2-small (embeddings) — cost-effective for nightly batch ingestion with high recall in vector search tests.

We've attached: acme-model-shortlist.pdf (shortlist + rationale), acme-benchmark-results.csv (latency & cost by sequence length), and prompt-set-v1.jsonl (proposed prompt set for your eval).

Proposed next steps:
- Acme to run a 1-week eval using the prompt set we attached (we can host an eval environment or ship a dedicated endpoint).
- Rishi to share benchmark links and run a quick latency smoke test against your sample dataset.
- Connor to coordinate contract/procurement cadence with Elena.

Can you confirm acceptance of the shortlist and whether you prefer Redwood-hosted eval or dedicated trial instances in your AWS account?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0119

John — quick answers + links inline.

On Mon, Mar 23, 2026 at 9:18 AM John Pritchard <john.pritchard@acme.com> wrote:
> 1) Latency envelope: that 95th perc ~180ms is tight for our UI; can you confirm that the redwood-realtime-13b numbers are on dedicated capacity or shared?

The redwood-realtime-13b numbers in acme-benchmark-results.csv are from a dedicated trial (pinned instance) running in our us-west-2 cluster with NVIDIA H100s using the low-latency execution path. Tail variance is ~25ms at 95th for the test prompt set we used (sequence len ~256 tokens). If you need tighter SLAs we can propose Dedicated (reserved) capacity — I'll include a config that pins two instances to keep p95 under 150ms.

> 2) Cost sensitivity: our procurement team will push for the lowest burn on embeddings. How much cheaper is open-embed-2-small vs the medium variant in your CSV?

Open-embed-2-small is ~55% lower per-embedding unit vs the medium in our cost model (see acme-benchmark-results.csv, column: "cost_per_1k_embeddings"). For nightly batch ingestion with 5M vectors/month, the small variant saves ~USD 3.2k/month.

> 3) Data residency/compliance: can we get SOC2 artifact access and a quick runbook on what logs are kept for private deployments?

We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and limited artifact access via our customer portal. For Private deployments we keep audit logs for: request metadata, KMS operations, and model version rollouts (default retention 365 days). We can customize retention windows for enterprise contracts.

Links:
- Benchmark CSV (shared): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcExampleBenchmark/view?usp=sharing
- Prompt/eval docs: https://docs.redwood.com/evals/acme/prompt-sets/v1
- SOC2 portal (request): https://redwood-compliance.example.com/request-artifacts

I'll provision a hosted eval endpoint for Acme tomorrow morning unless you'd prefer an AWS-side dedicated endpoint. Marissa — I'll attach a config snippet for the pinned instance proposal.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
